name: CleanSlate Centers
one_liner: In-person and telehealth addiction clinics offering Suboxone (buprenorphine) or Vivitrol plus counseling, in 7 states; takes Medicaid.
best_for: Adults with opioid use disorder who want buprenorphine (Suboxone) or Vivitrol
Adults who want medication for alcohol use disorder
People with Medicaid or Medicare in a state with a CleanSlate clinic
People who prefer in-person visits, with telehealth follow-ups at many sites
not_for: Anyone in crisis or overdose: call 911, or call or text 988
People who need medically supervised detox or residential treatment
People without a CleanSlate clinic in their state
People seeking methadone (CleanSlate is not an opioid treatment program)
short_description: Outpatient addiction clinics (medication plus counseling for opioid and alcohol use) in AZ, IN, KY, MA, OH, PA and WI.
long_description: CleanSlate Centers is a US chain of outpatient addiction medicine clinics, founded in Massachusetts in 2009, offering medication for opioid use disorder (buprenorphine/Suboxone, naltrexone/Vivitrol) and alcohol use disorder alongside counseling. Its site lists 65–70+ centers; its locations page lists Arizona, Indiana, Kentucky, Massachusetts, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin (older materials also mentioned Virginia and Texas). Many centers offer walk-in, phone and telehealth appointments, though care is clinic-based. It accepts Medicaid, Medicare, commercial insurance and self-pay; self-pay prices are not published. CleanSlate summarizes internal analyses (for example, higher retention among patients who attend counseling) on its website, but we found no peer-reviewed study of its clinics; the medications it uses are well supported by research in general.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance (Medicaid, Medicare, commercial); self-pay price not published
pricing.notes: Accepts Medicaid, Medicare, commercial insurance and out-of-pocket payment; staff help verify benefits before the first visit. No self-pay prices are published; ask your local center. Medication is billed by the pharmacy.

privacy.notes: Website privacy policy (read 2026-10-27) says CleanSlate does not sell or rent personal information, but its cookie policy says it uses targeting cookies that track sites users visit for ad campaigns, and the site's cookie list includes a Facebook advertising cookie; no general deletion right stated.

seo.meta_description: CleanSlate Centers provides outpatient addiction treatment combining medication-assisted treatment (MAT) with counseling for opioid and alcohol use disorders.

faqs.a: Yes, CleanSlate accepts Medicaid in most states where they operate. They also accept most commercial insurance plans. The goal is to remove financial barriers to addiction treatment. Call your local CleanSlate center to verify your specific coverage.

CleanSlate prescribes FDA-approved medications for addiction treatment including buprenorphine (Suboxone) for opioid use disorder and naltrexone (Vivitrol) for both opioid and alcohol use disorders. Medication is combined with counseling for comprehensive treatment.

faqs.q: Is CleanSlate treatment in-person or telehealth?
faqs.a: CleanSlate operates physical outpatient centers where you'll have initial visits. After stabilization, many patients can transition to telehealth follow-ups for convenience. The hybrid model combines the benefits of in-person care with telehealth accessibility.

faqs.q: How quickly can I start treatment at CleanSlate?
faqs.a: CleanSlate emphasizes low-barrier, quick access to treatment. Many centers can see patients within days rather than weeks. Walk-ins may be accepted depending on location. Call your nearest center for current availability.

primary_uses: Naltrexone (Vivitrol) injections for opioid or alcohol use disorder

patient_summary: You visit a CleanSlate clinic (or, at many sites, a telehealth appointment) where a clinician can prescribe buprenorphine (Suboxone) or naltrexone (Vivitrol) for opioid or alcohol use, with counseling. Clinics take Medicaid, Medicare and commercial insurance and help check your benefits before the first visit; self-pay is accepted but prices aren't published, so call your nearest center.

availability.note: Clinics in Arizona, Indiana, Kentucky, Massachusetts, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin per its locations page; telehealth visits at many centers.
